questions.stem: A train moving at 54 km/h crosses a man standing at a railway station in 10 seconds. What is the length of the train?

options.option_text: The length of the train is 120 metres
The length of the train is 150 metres
The length of the train is 175 metres
The length of the train is 200 metres

questions.explanation: Convert speed: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Length = speed × time = 15 × 10 = 150 m. Option D (200 m) is the most tempting trap — it uses 20 m/s, which corresponds to 72 km/h, not 54 km/h; a faulty km/h-to-m/s conversion is the root error.

questions.stem: Two trains, each 100 m long, run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h respectively. How many seconds will they take to completely cross each other?

options.option_text: They cross each other in 6 seconds
They cross each other in 8 seconds
They cross each other in 10 seconds
They cross each other in 12 seconds

questions.explanation: Relative speed (opposite directions) = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Total length to cover = 100 + 100 = 200 m. Time = 200 ÷ 25 = 8 seconds. Option C (10 s) is wrong — it divides 200 m by 20 m/s, implying a relative speed of 72 km/h, which ignores the correct sum of both speeds.

questions.stem: A train crosses a stationary pole in 12 seconds and a 180 m long platform in 24 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?

options.option_text: The speed of the train is 45 km/h
The speed of the train is 54 km/h
The speed of the train is 60 km/h
The speed of the train is 72 km/h

questions.explanation: Let train length = L. Speed is constant: L/12 = (L + 180)/24 → 24L = 12L + 2160 → L = 180 m. Speed = 180/12 = 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h. Option C (60 km/h ≈ 16.67 m/s) is wrong — that would require L = 16.67 × 12 = 200 m, but then the platform crossing would take (200+180)/16.67 = 22.8 s, not 24 s.

questions.stem: A 270 m long train overtakes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction and crosses him completely in 18 seconds. What is the actual speed of the train in km/h?

options.option_text: The speed of the train is 48 km/h
The speed of the train is 54 km/h
The speed of the train is 60 km/h
The speed of the train is 66 km/h

questions.explanation: Relative speed (same direction) = 270/18 = 15 m/s = 54 km/h. This is the speed of the train relative to the man, so actual train speed = 54 + 6 = 60 km/h. Option B (54 km/h) is the classic trap — it is the relative speed, not the train's absolute speed; candidates forget to add the man's walking speed.

questions.stem: A train normally completes a journey in 3 hours. If it travels at 4/5 of its usual speed due to a signal delay, by how many minutes will it arrive late?

options.option_text: The train will arrive 30 minutes late
The train will arrive 36 minutes late
The train will arrive 45 minutes late
The train will arrive 60 minutes late

questions.explanation: At 4/5 speed, time taken = (5/4) × 3 = 15/4 hours = 3 hr 45 min. Delay = 45 minutes. Option B (36 min) is the distractor for a 5/6 speed reduction [(6/5 × 3 − 3) × 60 = 36 min], which is a different fraction entirely — examiners often substitute nearby fractions to create plausible wrong options.

questions.stem: Two trains start simultaneously from stations A and B towards each other. After crossing, the train from A takes 4 hours to reach B, and the train from B takes 9 hours to reach A. What is the ratio of the speed of the train from A to the speed of the train from B?

options.option_text: The ratio of their speeds is 2 : 3
The ratio of their speeds is 3 : 2
The ratio of their speeds is 4 : 9
The ratio of their speeds is 9 : 4

questions.explanation: Let meeting time = t, speeds = vA and vB. After crossing: vB·t/vA = 4 and vA·t/vB = 9. Multiplying: t² = 36, so t = 6. Then vA/vB = 9/6 = 3/2, i.e., 3:2. Equivalently, speed ratio = √(B's after-crossing time) : √(A's after-crossing time) = √9 : √4 = 3:2. Option C (4:9) is the most common error — it reports the ratio of after-crossing times directly instead of taking square roots.

questions.stem: Train X departs station P at 7:00 AM towards Q at 60 km/h. Train Y departs station Q at 8:00 AM towards P at 90 km/h. If the distance PQ is 300 km, how far from P do the two trains meet?

options.option_text: They meet at a point 144 km from station P
They meet at a point 150 km from station P
They meet at a point 156 km from station P
They meet at a point 160 km from station P

questions.explanation: By 8:00 AM, X has covered 60 km, leaving a gap of 240 km between the trains. Combined closing speed = 60 + 90 = 150 km/h. Time to meet = 240/150 = 8/5 hr. Distance X covers after 8 AM = 60 × 8/5 = 96 km. Total distance from P = 60 + 96 = 156 km. Option A (144 km) is a trap — 144 km is Y's distance from Q (90 × 8/5 = 144), not from P; the correct distance from P = 300 − 144 = 156 km.
